click | dblclick | doubleclick | focus: require selector.

click/dblclick: the target is probed until it is present, has a layout box, is enabled, is what a hit test finds at its click point (the centre of its visible box, scrolled into view) and has stopped moving, then a trusted move/press/release is dispatched there; dblclick sends two clicks then dblclick, as a person does. The wait is at most 8s (never past the run's budget), and a target that never becomes clickable fails that action with the reason: matches no element (with a hint when the page has iframes - selectors reach the top document only), not visible (display: none, visibility, no box), stayed disabled, covered at (x, y) by a named element (dialog, backdrop, toast, sticky bar), or kept moving. A target's own label or an ancestor of a pointer-events:none icon taking the hit counts as the target. type/focus wait for a box the same way.
type: requires selector and text; sends trusted keys.

fill: requires selector and text (including intentionally empty ""); selector must target an enabled, writable textarea or text/search/email/tel/url/password input, or a date input with a valid ISO date value. Date values are checked with a detached native date input before actions run, so locale-specific display strings are refused. The same preflighted node must remain usable; fill uses the native value setter, dispatches bubbling input then change, and verifies that connected node's settled value.

select: requires selector and value (including intentionally empty ""); selector must target an enabled select whose first matching option (the one the native setter selects) is enabled. The same preflighted node must remain usable; select dispatches bubbling input then change and verifies the actual selected option and settled value.
key: requires key. scroll: requires selector or y. wait: optional non-negative ms (default 300).
sequential_actions: true: each target is waited for (up to 8s), so a control rendered after a fetch needs no explicit wait.
